title: Signal map: product/eng/applied-ml roadmap sync (scratch)
summary: Working scratch to translate product priorities into a simple signal map for the upcoming cross-functional roadmap sync. Aim: surface hard tradeoffs (latency vs cost vs quality) and identify 2 quick wins + 2 risky bets we can align on for Q2 planning.
meeting_details: 2026-03-12 11:00-12:00 PT | 60m | Attendees: Maya (PM), Riley (Eng lead), Noah (Applied ML), Priya (SWE-infra), Evan (note taker) — informal, bring concrete asks & tolerances.
agenda_items: 5m: Quick framing — north star and constraints
20m: Walk signal map + three candidate initiatives
20m: Surface engineering cost/latency implications and ML quality risk
10m: Decide immediate next steps and owners
prep_todo: Maya: bring prioritized use-cases with expected QPS and latency SLOs
Riley: bring rough GPU-week estimate for each initiative (p50)
Noah: supply sample eval metric delta estimates for candidate model swaps
Priya: confirm Dedicated capacity availability windows and limits
Evan: prepare the one-page signal map (this doc) and send before meeting
discussion_notes:
Framing: product wants 2x better user-perceived latency on chat flows while keeping incremental token cost under 15% for hosted tier. Engineering flagged that achieving <50ms median requires kernel-level changes + possible batching changes that increase tail latency on small requests. Applied ML flagged quality regressions for 7B->4B quantized variants on out-of-distribution prompts — requires targeted eval sets.

Candidate initiatives discussed:
- Initiative A: 'Low-latency fast-path' (optimize attention kernels + lighter quantization profile). Product impact: high latency reduction for chat; Cost: medium-high (dev + infra); ML risk: medium (needs eval).
- Initiative B: 'Adaptive routing by SLA' (route tiered requests to cheaper model unless flagged). Product impact: medium (cost down), Cost: low infra changes but needs routing policy; ML risk: low if fallback rules conservative.
- Initiative C: 'Prefix KV caching + shared-session' (cache hot prefixes to reduce tokens). Product impact: medium-high for repeat queries; Cost: medium; ML risk: negligible but complexity ops-heavy.

Key tensions surfaced: product wants aggressive latency gains by EOY; eng wants staged rollout with canaries; ML wants more eval coverage before wider quantization. Consensus lean is to pursue A as a guarded bet with B as the safety net and C as quick win grooming into Dedicated customers first.

Parking lot: need numbers from billing on per-token cost elasticity with caching, and a small user-study to validate perceived latency improvements.
action_items: Riley: produce p50/p95 GPU-week estimate matrix for Initiatives A/B/C — due 2026-03-19
Noah: run targeted evals on the 1200-prompt OOD set for the proposed quant profiles and share delta table — due 2026-03-18
Maya: draft updated product ask with 3 SLO tiers and per-tier traffic split suggestions — due 2026-03-17
Priya: confirm Dedicated pool headroom and earliest possible pilot window; list constraints — due 2026-03-16
Evan: consolidate meeting notes + signal map PNG and post to confluence + ping stakeholders — due 2026-03-13
decisions: Pursue Initiative A as the primary engineering effort but gate by Noah's eval results (if quality drop > 3% on key metrics, postpone broad rollout)
Spin up Initiative B as a fallback routing policy prototype to be ready for canary phase
Treat Initiative C as a near-term low-risk experiment for Dedicated customers only
risks_and_assumptions: Assume Dedicated customers will tolerate slightly higher per-request complexity for caching approaches. Risk that quantization artifacts on edge cases are underestimated — require human-in-the-loop failure detection for first 2 weeks of rollout. Also assume we can get billing delta numbers within 3 business days (may be optimistic).
